# QS-CFW-2117-10 - Quality specification - valve body CFW-2117-10 (F316)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-2117-10

Scope
- This specification defines acceptance criteria and inspection methods for forged valve body CFW-2117-10 (F316) manufactured at Plant P2. Applies to finished forgings prior to heat treatment handoff and final machining release.

Requirements table

| Feature | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material identification | F316 per purchase order |
| Hardness | The hardness range for valve body CFW-2117-10 (CFW-2117-10) is 39-44 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-2117-10 (CFW-2117-10) is ±0.09 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-2117-10 (CFW-2117-10) is 14.5 kg. |
| Visual finish | Free of laps, seams, and surface cracking visible at normal shop lighting |

Inspection method
- Identification: Verify heat lot and material traceability against stamping and mill certificates.
- Hardness: Perform hardness testing on each lot using a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester. Record readings and verify they fall within The hardness range for valve body CFW-2117-10 (CFW-2117-10) is 39-44 HRC. Test locations shall be representative of the component body and recorded on the inspection report.
- Dimensional: Inspect bore diameter using calibrated bore gauge or coordinate measurement equipment. Confirm bore conforms to the bore diameter tolerance for valve body CFW-2117-10 (CFW-2117-10) is ±0.09 mm. Document measured values and gauge identification.
- Weight: Weigh each forging and confirm compliance with The maximum forging weight for valve body CFW-2117-10 (CFW-2117-10) is 14.5 kg. Record serial/part number with weight result.
- Visual: Perform final visual inspection under standard shop lighting; record disposition.

Nonconformance handling
- Segregate nonconforming parts and tag with NCR. Record the nonconformance, root cause, and proposed disposition. Rework permitted only if documented and approved by Quality Engineering; otherwise scrap. Release for shipment requires Quality sign-off after corrective action.
